# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Flight for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## A Field on the Sand Flight began in the 2160s as a landing field and a freight shed on open sand, chartered under the United Americas as a way station for ships working the Neroid Sector. Cargo came down from orbit, waited for a buyer and went back up. The crews who handled it needed bunks, then a canteen, then room for their families. Pilots logged it as Flight Field. The field was paved over long ago, but the name stayed.
## The Tower - In the early 2170s the charter holders stopped building outwards and started building up: nine floors above ground, a basement under them and a landing pad on the roof. - Homes, shops, clinics, hydroponics and offices share the same stairwells and cargo lifts. Plenty of residents go a whole season without stepping outside. - Ships still come in at three points: the West Hangar at street level, the indoor hangar on the sixth floor and the rooftop pad.
## The City Around It The streets around the tower were laid out before anyone lived on them: paved roads, sidewalks, street lights and trees planted in imported soil, a city built to look like one. Past the last block the sand starts again.
## The Sixth Floor The Administration, the Colonial Marshal Bureau, the Foreman's office and the Weyland-Yutani liaison all keep offices along one corridor of the sixth floor, a short walk from the indoor hangar. Residents call it [italic]the Sixth[/italic], and when a decision lands on them, they say it came down from the Sixth.
## The Hard Lessons The tower went up fast, and a building this tall forgives nothing. The open wells that let light down through the middle floors have taken more lives than any machine, and there are falls on the record from every floor. Sand works into the filters, lifts stall between floors and the disposal chutes are no place for anyone. Every one of them has names attached in our archive.
## The Press The Herald has been filed from Flight since 2173, first as a sheet taped inside the cargo lifts, now here on the net. The job has not changed: write down what happens on every floor, not only on the Sixth.
